s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity weakness with sensory changes and autonomic dysfunction
salient_findings: Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
Sensation to light touch reduced in feet
key_facts: Weakness began in proximal left leg and gradually involved right leg and both hands
Worsening numbness and tingling in feet
Denies pain, flank pain, hematuria, fevers, visual changes, speech or swallowing difficulty
Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
Sensation to light touch reduced in feet
Reflexes 2+ in upper extremities and absent at knees and ankles
Bladder catheterization yielded 1.8 L of retained urine
Urine negative for protein or bacteria
CSF analysis revealed protein 175 mg/dL, glucose 105 mg/dL, 1 WBC, 0 RBC
Lyme serology, autoimmune panel, and paraneoplastic antibody panel negative
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrated chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy with superimposed chronic lumbosacral plexopathy
MRI of pelvis showed bilateral femoral nerve enlargement without enhancement

shortlist.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes with CSF protein elevation and demyelinating features on electromyography and nerve conduction studies

shortlist.label: Diabetic amyotrophy
shortlist.why_kept: History of type II diabetes and progressive lower-extremity weakness with atrophy, consistent with diabetic amyotrophy

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral femoral nerve enlargement on MRI and clinical features of lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes

shortlist.label: Multifocal motor neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness with atrophy and demyelinating features on electromyography and nerve conduction studies

shortlist.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness with atrophy and upper motor neuron signs, although less likely given sensory involvement

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of progressive lower-extremity weakness, although less likely given chronic course and absence of antecedent infection

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Unintentional weight loss and progressive lower-extremity weakness, although paraneoplastic panel was negative

shortlist.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes, although autoimmune panel was negative

raw.rationale: The patient's 1-year history of progressive lower-extremity weakness, significant weight loss, and worsening numbness and tingling in feet, along with the presence of type II diabetes, are consistent with diabetic amyotrophy. The electromyography and nerve conduction studies also support this diagnosis, showing a chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy with superimposed chronic lumbosacral plexopathy, which is characteristic of diabetic amyotrophy.

rejected.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
rejected.why: While the patient's electromyography and nerve conduction studies show demyelination, the absence of a significant response to autoimmune panels and the presence of type II diabetes make diabetic amyotrophy a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy
rejected.why: This diagnosis is a subset of diabetic amyotrophy, and the patient's symptoms and test results are more consistent with the broader diagnosis of diabetic amyotrophy.

rejected.label: Multifocal motor neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and test results do not show a clear multifocal pattern, and the presence of sensory symptoms makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and test results do not show significant upper motor neuron signs, and the presence of sensory symptoms makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms have been progressive over 1 year, which is not consistent with the typical acute onset of Guillain-Barré syndrome.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's paraneoplastic antibody panel was negative, and there is no other evidence of an underlying malignancy.

rejected.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's test results do not show significant evidence of vasculitis, and the presence of type II diabetes makes diabetic amyotrophy a more likely diagnosis.
